fields.hero_prompt: Build an HVAC inspection form my technicians fill out on a tablet, with checks that change for a furnace, heat pump, or AC.

faq_plan.q: What is an HVAC inspection form?
How do I create an HVAC inspection form?

plan.angle: The results for this query are downloadable HVAC checklists (PDF, Excel, Etsy listings) and field-service vendors' template pages. None shows the form working on a call: a technician picking the equipment type, typing readings, photographing a failed part, the customer signing, and a manager seeing which maintenance plan customers are overdue. This page shows a working HVAC inspection form at four moments (a residential spring tune-up, a quarterly rooftop unit round, a failed furnace safety check, the maintenance plan register), every inspection saved to a database the company owns. Check items are quoted from ENERGY STAR's maintenance checklist; no code, safety or efficiency claims.
tab_stories: At Cavendale Heating and Air, technician Florian Wynkoop runs a 16-point spring tune-up on a split system, replaces the filter, the homeowner signs on his tablet, and the report is emailed before he leaves.

At Ruskwood Properties, facilities tech Casimir Starkweather checks the 6 rooftop units on one office building each quarter; 5 pass and RTU-4 is flagged for a worn belt, which emails property manager Henrietta Pridmore.

At Tallis Creek Mechanical, technician Rutger Emmerich finds a cracked heat exchanger on a fall furnace check; the form asks for a photo, marks the furnace Unsafe and posts to service manager Leocadia Brunell in Slack.
At Pennwick Comfort Services, the maintenance plan register lists 140 plan customers for the fall heating check: 96 done, 31 booked and 13 overdue, with the overdue ones at the top.

claims_to_source: ENERGY STAR: check the cooling system in the spring and the heating system in the fall
ENERGY STAR: tighten all electrical connections and measure voltage and current on motors
ENERGY STAR: check all gas (or oil) connections, gas pressure, burner combustion and heat exchanger
ENERGY STAR: inspect, clean, or change air filters once a month
ENERGY STAR: check and inspect the condensate drain
